Veribench/20_html_escape.lean.content: import Mathlib /-! # HTML escaping Lean formalization of the classic `html.escape` routine (Python's `html` library): replace `&`, `<` and `>` by HTML-safe entities, and, when `quote` is true, also replace `"` by `"` and `'` by `'`. `&` is replaced first and inserted text is not scanned again, so a single call does not double-escape. Strings are sequences of Unicode code points, matching Python 3 `str`. Non-`str` inputs are outside this type; Python would raise `TypeError` there. -/ namespace «20_html_escape» open String set_option linter.unusedSimpArgs false set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 abbrev ampR : List Char := "&".data abbrev ltR : List Char := "<".data abbrev gtR : List Char := ">".data abbrev quotR : List Char := """.data abbrev aposR : List Char := "'".data /-- Python `str.replace` for a one-character pattern. The replacement is not re-scanned. -/ def replaceChar (pat : Char) (repl : List Char) : List Char → List Char | [] => [] | c :: cs => (if c = pat then repl else [c]) ++ replaceChar pat repl cs /-- One original character, encoded the way `html.escape` encodes it. -/ def encodeChar (quote : Bool) (c : Char) : List Char := if c = '&' then ampR else if c = '<' then ltR else if c = '>' then gtR else if quote = true ∧ c = '"' then quotR else if quote = true ∧ c = '\'' then aposR else [c] /-- Successive replacements, in the same order as Python's `html.escape`. -/ def escapeData (quote : Bool) (cs : List Char) : List Char := let core := replaceChar '>' gtR (replaceChar '<' ltR (replaceChar '&' ampR cs)) if quote = true then replaceChar '\'' aposR (replaceChar '"' quotR core) else core def escape (s : String) (quote : Bool := true) : String := ⟨escapeData quote s.data⟩ /-- Entry point checked by the Python driver. Lean's `String` is that domain, and `quote` may be either Boolean. -/ def Pre (_s : String) (_quote : Bool) : Prop := True /-! ## Lemmas toward the character-wise specification -/ theorem
